security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline command examples. Confirmed risks remain for force-killing processes on port 3030 and sourcing shell startup files. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious network intent was found.

remediation.issue: Force-kill port cleanup can terminate unrelated local processes.
remediation.suggestion: Replace direct kill -9 guidance with process inspection, owner verification, graceful termination, and explicit user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Sourcing shell startup files can execute hidden local shell code.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid automatic source commands. Ask the user to open a new shell or approve reloading a specific startup file.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded absolute paths reduce portability and can point to unexpected local scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Document required environment variables or project-relative paths instead of personal home-directory paths.

content.user_title: Manage Local Dev Servers with PM2
content.value_statement: Local development servers often fail because ports are busy, processes crash, or logs are hard to find. This skill gives structured PM2 workflows for reliable start, restart, and troubleshooting steps.
actual_capabilities: Provides PM2 start, stop, restart, status, and log workflows for Empathy Ledger.
Documents ACT ecosystem server management commands and project port assignments.
Explains how to recover from local address-in-use errors on port 3030.
Shows when to use PM2 instead of a direct development server command.
Connects local server management with Supabase, migrations, and test scripts.
limitations: The workflow is specific to Empathy Ledger and ACT local development paths.
It assumes Node, PM2, and the required project repositories already exist locally.
Some cleanup steps can terminate local processes if used without verification.
It does not provide Windows-specific server management instructions.

use_cases.title: Recover a Blocked Local Port
use_cases.description: Find and clear the process using a development port, then restart Empathy Ledger with PM2.

use_cases.title: Run the ACT Project Set
use_cases.description: Start, restart, stop, and inspect multiple ACT projects through the documented ecosystem workflow.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Test Session
use_cases.description: Confirm the server is running, restart after schema changes, and review logs before testing APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Start the Local Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the local Empathy Ledger development server and confirm it is responsive.

prompt_templates.title: Restart After Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Restart Empathy Ledger after my latest changes, wait for startup, and check recent logs for errors.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Busy Port
prompt_templates.prompt: Port 3030 is already in use. Identify the cause, confirm the cleanup step, then start the server with PM2.

prompt_templates.title: Verify the Full Ecosystem
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the full ACT ecosystem, verify each project status, and summarize any failed services with next steps.

output_examples.output: The server was restarted through PM2. Startup completed, and recent logs did not show a blocking error.
The process using port 3030 was identified. After confirmation, the port was cleared and the server was started again.
The local server was checked first. It responded successfully, so API testing can proceed with current logs available.

best_practices: Confirm process ownership before terminating anything on a local port.
Review PM2 logs after every restart or failed startup.
Keep documented paths and port numbers aligned with the current project setup.
anti_patterns: Do not force-kill a port on a shared machine without checking the process first.
Do not assume the hardcoded project paths exist on every developer machine.
Do not use PM2 when direct terminal output is required for active debugging.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages local Empathy Ledger and ACT development server workflows using PM2.

faq.question: Does it install PM2 automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents the PM2 installation command and assumes the user approves setup steps.

faq.question: Can it fix address-in-use errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to find the process on a port and restart the server after cleanup.

faq.question: Is this skill portable across projects?
faq.answer: Only partly. Many paths, ports, and names are specific to the ACT and Empathy Ledger setup.

faq.question: What tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects a Unix-like shell, Node, PM2, and access to the relevant local project directories.

faq.question: What should users verify before cleanup commands?
faq.answer: Users should verify the process ID, owner, port, and project before terminating any process.
